name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd
title: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd - 540716 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: ICICI Lombard FY26 PBT rose 10.2% to ₹36.59bn and 1/n PAT 10.5% to ₹27.72bn; Q4 GDPI grew 18.2% but FY26 GDPI grew only 7.0%.
summary.overview: FY26 profit grew double digits despite a ₹0.55bn wage code charge, with Q4 1/n PAT up 7.3% to ₹5.47bn. Top-line growth was 7.0% for FY26 versus the industry's 9.2%, with commercial lines lagging (5.4%) and retail health (51.1%) and Q4 motor (15.0%) accelerating. Management flagged intensifying commercial and fire competition, a Motor TP loss ratio it says is overdue for repricing, and a transition to Ind AS starting FY27 with a plan to seek forbearance. Solvency stayed high at 2.67x and the final dividend was ₹7.00 per share (₹13.50 total).

+10.5% YoY vs ₹25.08 bn; ₹28.14 bn ex wage code
vs 19.1% FY25; 18.1% ex wage code; Q4 FY26 13.3% vs 14.5%

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: FY26 growth 5.4% vs industry 12.2% (H1 6.5% vs 14.2%; H2 3.8% vs 9.6%). Market share fell about 0.7-0.8 pp, per management, and fire pricing pressure drove the slowdown.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: FY26 growth 7.6% vs industry 9.2%; H2 12.0% vs 10.5%, Q4 15.0% vs 10.0%. Portfolio mix: private car 52.8%, two-wheeler 25.4%, commercial vehicle 21.8%. Full-year Motor loss ratio about 66.3%, within the 65-67% comfort range.

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: Growth 51.1% in FY26 vs industry 19.9%; market share rose from 3.3% to 4.1%. Long-term share of new retail health business rose to 42.1% from 28.5%. Retail indemnity loss ratio 64.6% for FY26 (Q4 57.6%).

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Growth 11.0% in FY26 with 8.7% market share. Employer-employee loss ratio 91.9% for FY26 (Q4 98.1%).

segments.name: Overall health
segments.commentary: Health growth 20.0% vs industry 15.4% on a 1/n basis; Q4 growth 38.2% vs industry 20.5%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects industry motor growth in the higher single digits for FY27 and expects Q1 and Q2 FY27 to start positively, though it did not give numeric guidance.
Commercial industry growth could be single digit in FY27 because of fire pricing pressure; April 1, 2026 renewals are being reported at a discount.

Ind AS: IRDAI mandates Ind AS from April 1, 2026. The company intends to seek forbearance for the first year and will submit quarterly pro forma Ind AS numbers from Q1 FY27. Management guided to a 300-450 bps combined ratio decline in the adoption year, with economic value converging over time.
Dividend policy: about 25% of PAT on average; FY26 payout of ₹13.50 per share is roughly 25% of PAT. Solvency may be used for growth, subject to the transition to risk-based capital.
Motor TP: management hopes for an industry TP price hike, which it calls overdue, with the industry Motor TP loss ratio near 85%.
capex_capacity: Crop insurance: current crop exposure is about half of the level of two years ago; the company will not chase crop targets and will select risks, and it plans to expand beyond one state if commercially sensible.
IL OneForce enterprise platform is used by over 10,000 sales staff and is set to cover all 15,000+ employees.
Investment leverage (net of borrowings) fell to 3.48x from 3.60x in Q3 FY26.
demand_pricing: Retail vehicle sales (VAHAN) FY26: private cars +11.9%, two-wheelers +13.2%, commercial vehicles +12.9%; H2 private car +17.8%, two-wheeler +21.5%, commercial vehicle +20.2%.
Commercial competition has intensified, especially in fire in H2 FY26; reinsurance renewals for FY27 were soft.
Industry Motor combined ratio 128.1% for 9M FY26 vs 123.8% 9M FY25, driven by pricing pressure. Industry overall CoR 119.3% for 9M FY26 vs 113.2%.
Company 10-year (FY16-FY25) average combined ratio 102.9% vs industry 115.3%; average realised yield 8.7%; average ROE 19.1% vs industry 4.0%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 Motor TP loss ratio much lower, and why is the crop loss ratio negative? Has IFRS PAT been quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to judge Motor as a category over full year (66.3%, range 65-67%) and reserving philosophy is unchanged. Crop was booked mostly in Q2 at about 100% loss ratio, and the Q4 release reflects favourable experience. No Ind AS PAT quantification yet; the company will return with CoR and ROE impact.

qa_highlights.question: Solvency is high at 2.7x; can excess capital be deployed via dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Solvency 1 (exposure-based capital) and a pending risk-based capital transition. It will use some solvency for growth as growth returns, and continues a dividend policy of about 25% of PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Health loss ratio split between retail and group, and Motor TP price hike outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Employer-employee loss ratio was 98.1% in Q4 and 91.9% for FY26; retail indemnity was 57.6% in Q4 and 64.6% for FY26, with a 65-70% target range. Industry Motor TP loss ratio is about 85%, and a price hike is overdue but not in the company's control.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company claw back commercial market share and sustain 16% H2 growth into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 share fell about 0.7-0.8 pp from 13.7% and it will be selective, not chasing volume. It expects an industry growth slowdown in commercial, possibly single digit, and was confident of positive Q1 and Q2 but declined to predict the H2 run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of H2 motor outperformance and FY27 outlook, and the Motor TP reserve and CV growth question?
qa_highlights.answer: New vehicle sales grew 18.8% for the company vs 13.4% for renewals; retention improved about 5%. CV share of book remained around 22%, with cost of acquisition and a fleet management system cited. Management declined to give the Motor TP reserve figure as a useful metric.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the commission (EOM) tightening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tightening applied uniformly would benefit ICICI Lombard, which says it has stayed within expense-of-management limits. It favours a single-slab EOM structure and awaits regulatory direction.

risks_watch: Commercial lines share loss and fire pricing pressure, with April 1, 2026 renewals reported at a discount.
Motor TP loss ratio sensitivity and a possible long-tail reserve build; industry Motor combined ratio 128.1% (9M FY26).
Crop insurance expansion beyond one state and the terms of the new crop framework.
Ind AS transition in FY27 (forbearance sought); combined ratio and ROE comparability to be disclosed.
Equity portfolio MTM (₹0.49 bn impairment in Q4) and solvency at 2.67x.
Geopolitical and energy-price shock from West Asia conflict that could slow auto sales and savings behaviour.
Possible EOM and commission regulation changes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, retail health, and the Q4 growth rebound, but guarded on the commercial outlook, the Motor TP cycle, and the macro (West Asia conflict). Management avoided numeric FY27 guidance and deflected detailed questions on the crop loss ratio and Ind AS PAT impact.
key_quotes: It is a welcome sign if it comes out, we have always also mentioned the fact that we believe the expense of management should be on a single slab basis so that there's clarity of execution and let the market forces decide as to what works for each one of them in every single business line.
The combined ratio which I just spoke about for the nine months stayed at 128 clearly not a workable one.
We are very well placed as an institution in terms of what practices we have to counter any such measures that come up in the market.
The overall CoR for private players remained relatively flattish from 111.2% for the period 9M FY2025 to 111.5% for the period 9M FY2026.
And that's what Gopal is referring to when he's saying that we have a delta of higher retention of our customers.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 company growth guidance; management expects industry motor growth in higher single digits and commercial industry growth in single digits, with Q1-Q2 FY27 motor starting positively, but no capacity or order backing is given, while Q4 GDPI grew 18.2% and FY26 GDPI grew 7.0%.
